newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The caretaker government has approved another amendment in the electoral laws giving suo moto powers to the election tribunals to debar defaulters of loans, taxes and utility charges from contesting the general.

- More than 3,400 employees of the state-run Karachi Transport Corporation will be rendered jobless and 100 buses will disappear from the city roads as the corporation will cease to function on Tuesday after operating for 20 years.
- The federal cabinet has increased prices of natural gas by 15 percent for domestic, commercial and industrial consumers from January 1, 1997, a federal minister said.
- A high level mission of the European Commission will visit Pakistan soon to evaluate the working of the state-run Federal Bureau of Statistics and help improve the quality of its output.
- The Indian Government has agreed to allow Pakistani importers to participate in the international tender floated by India for the sale of one million bales of cotton.
- The World Bank has decided to cancel loans for projects in which the borrowers were found to be involved in corrupt or fraudulent practices.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has issued a list of loan defaulters and those individuals and companies who got their loans written off.
- Sugar production declined by 17.9 percent to 2.44 million tonnes during 1995/96 (July-June) from 2.98 million tonnes in 1994/95.

- Pakistan's liquid foreign exchange reserves, excluding bullion reserves, would be around $800 million by December 31, Shahid Javed Burki advisor to the Prime Minister on Finance and Economic Affairs said.
